bugs.symptom: Canvas drag-pan attaches window pointermove/pointerup listeners; if the canvas unmounts mid-drag (e.g. navigation) before pointerup, the listeners are never removed.
bugs.root_cause: Drag listeners self-removed only on pointerup, with no unmount cleanup path.
bugs.fix: useViewport tracks the active detach fn in detachDragRef; a useEffect unmount cleanup calls it, and a new drag detaches any stale one first. (src/features/tree-canvas/hooks/useViewport.ts)
bugs.mitigation: Single detach ref reused for both pointerup and unmount; impossible to leave a dangling listener.
bugs.regression_test: covered indirectly by tree-canvas selection tests; pan/zoom e2e deferred with iteration 3

bugs.symptom: BookService.duplicateBook spread each node shallowly ({ ...n, id }), so the copy shared the SAME nested position/decor/pnj/monster/trap object references as the source — the spec promised a deep copy. Latent: an in-place edit of a sub-object on one book would leak into the other.
bugs.root_cause: Shallow object spread only clones top-level node fields; nested objects stay shared references. Surfaced in the tech-lead review of the book-library iter-1 diff.
bugs.fix: duplicateBook now deep-clones each node via a JSON round-trip (the exact clone here — the book is JSON-serialised by PersistenceService anyway) before reassigning its remapped id. (src/brain/BookService.ts duplicateBook)
bugs.mitigation: Regression test asserts the copy's decor/position are toEqual but NOT toBe (===) the source's, so a future shallow-copy regression fails the suite.
bugs.regression_test: src/brain/BookService.test.ts — 'duplicateBook deep-clones nested node sub-objects (no shared references with the source)'

bugs.symptom: The in-place rename Escape-cancel path (a named iter-1 goal) had no test, leaving the no-commit-on-Escape contract unverified and brittle to refactors.
bugs.root_cause: Coverage gap, flagged in the tech-lead review.
bugs.fix: Added an integration test that types into the rename input then presses Escape and asserts the title is unchanged and edit mode exits. Confirms React does not fire onBlur when the input unmounts on setEditing(false), so Escape does not double-commit via the onBlur handler.
bugs.mitigation: The asymmetric trim comparison was also tightened (commitRename compares against book.title.trim()), so a re-commit of a visually-same value never fires a redundant book:updated.
bugs.regression_test: src/features/book-library/tests/library.test.tsx — 'cancels an in-place rename with Escape, leaving the title unchanged'

bugs.symptom: useViewport re-declared its own `Viewport` interface, duplicating the brain UIPreferencesService `Viewport`. Two structurally-identical types for one concept can silently drift (a field added to one and not the other).
bugs.root_cause: The hook predates UIPreferencesService and owned its local type; iter 3 introduced the canonical brain type without collapsing the duplicate. Flagged in the tech-lead review.
bugs.fix: useViewport now imports `Viewport` from brain (re-exporting the type) and the local interface was deleted. (src/features/tree-canvas/hooks/useViewport.ts)
bugs.mitigation: One source of truth for the viewport shape (brain); the hook references it, so a future field lands once.
bugs.regression_test: covered by existing useViewport-driven TreeCanvas tests (zoom persistence); tsc enforces the shared shape

bugs.symptom: The live viewport is seed-once via a lazy useState initializer and does not re-seed when bookId changes; a future in-editor book→book switch would keep the previous book's pan/zoom.
bugs.root_cause: Latent (not reachable today — every editor entry mounts EditorScreen fresh from home). Flagged as an insurance fix in the tech-lead review.
bugs.fix: EditorScreen is keyed by route.bookId at the composition root (App.tsx), so a book switch remounts the shell and the viewport re-seeds from the new book's persisted prefs.
bugs.mitigation: The seed-once contract is made explicit by the key; reactive prefs (view-mode/positions) were already safe via external-store hooks.
bugs.regression_test: src/features/tree-canvas/tests/TreeCanvas.test.tsx — 'restores persisted view state on reload (a fresh App over the same store)'

bugs.symptom: The KR-022/093 non-sync guarantee (UI prefs never reach the cloud queue) was pinned only structurally (key namespace, service wired over local), with no test proving a prefs write leaves the cloud queue empty.
bugs.root_cause: Coverage gap on the slice's headline contract, flagged in the tech-lead review.
bugs.fix: Added a test that runs createBrain with a never-resolving transport, writes viewport+view-mode+position via brain.uiPreferences, and asserts sync.pendingCount() === 0 and the CLOUDSYNC_QUEUE_KEY is absent.
bugs.mitigation: A leaked write through the sync decorator would stick the never-resolving push and fail the assertion, so a future mis-wiring is caught.
bugs.regression_test: src/brain/UIPreferencesService.test.ts — 'is NEVER cloud-synced: prefs writes do not enter the cloud queue (KR-022/093)'

bugs.symptom: In the Décor editor, authoring a reveal text under « Écouter » then switching to the « Fouiller » tab showed exactly the same text — the user read it as React failing to re-render.
bugs.root_cause: NOT a render bug — React did re-render (the field label correctly changed from « Ce que le joueur entend » to « Ce que le joueur trouve »). DecorConfig stored a SINGLE shared `reveal`, so écouter and fouiller read/wrote the same field; switching the interaction tab carried the text across because it was literally the same data.
bugs.fix: Made the reveal PER INTERACTION: DecorConfig.reveals?: Partial<Record<DecorInteraction, DecorReveal>>; DecorEditor reads/writes reveals[interaction] (RevealEditor now bound to the current interaction's reveal). The legacy single `reveal` is migrated on read (revealsOf attributes it to the node's current interaction, KR-090) and dropped on the next canonical write. (src/brain/types.ts, src/features/action-decor/utils/takeables.ts revealsOf, src/features/action-decor/components/DecorEditor.tsx)
bugs.mitigation: Regression test drives écouter→fouiller→écouter and asserts each field is independent and both reveals persist; a migration test asserts an old single-reveal book maps onto the current interaction.
bugs.regression_test: src/features/action-decor/tests/decor.test.tsx — 'keeps Écouter and Fouiller reveal texts INDEPENDENT when switching tabs (BUG-007)' + 'migrates a legacy single shared reveal onto the node current interaction (KR-090)'

bugs.symptom: Tech-lead review: EquipmentEffect was a flat interface with weapon? and protection? both optional, allowing TypeScript to accept { kind: 'arme', protection: 'cuir' } without error — a structurally invalid object that the runtime would guard by kind but could not be caught at compile time.
bugs.root_cause: The interface used a union literal kind: 'arme' | 'protection' with optional sibling fields, which is a structural union not a discriminated one. TypeScript cannot narrow optional fields by discriminant alone.
bugs.fix: Changed EquipmentEffect to a discriminated union type: { kind: 'arme'; weapon: WeaponId } | { kind: 'protection'; protection: ProtectionId }. Updated ObjectEditor.tsx to use narrowed access (equip.kind === 'arme' ? equip.weapon : DEFAULT_WEAPON) instead of equip?.weapon ?? WEAPON_VALUES[0].
bugs.mitigation: KR-117 registries should always be discriminated unions, not structural unions. When the kind discriminant determines which fields are present, use type X = A | B, not interface X with optional sibling fields.

bugs.symptom: Tech-lead review: ObjectEditor used WEAPON_VALUES[0] and PROTECTION_VALUES[0] as fallback defaults for the equipment effect selects instead of named constants. If the registry order changed, the default would silently shift.
bugs.root_cause: DEFAULT_WEAPON was exported from equipment.ts but not imported in ObjectEditor. DEFAULT_PROTECTION did not exist at all.
bugs.fix: Added DEFAULT_PROTECTION = 'cuir' to equipment.ts and brain/index.ts. Updated ObjectEditor.tsx to import and use DEFAULT_WEAPON/DEFAULT_PROTECTION instead of WEAPON_VALUES[0]/PROTECTION_VALUES[0].
bugs.mitigation: KR-117 registries must expose a DEFAULT_X constant alongside WEAPON_VALUES/PROTECTION_VALUES. New registries should always include a named default; callers should always import the named constant, never index the values array.

bugs.symptom: A monster selected from the library showed 'Aucune' in the Capacité spéciale field instead of its actual capacity (e.g. 'Vol' for a Gobelin). Observed immediately after the capacity registry (KR-117) landed.
bugs.root_cause: MonsterLibraryService.seedDefaults() has a one-time guard (MONSTER_LIBRARY_SEEDED_KEY). When the capacity registry shipped, the guard key was already set for existing users, so seedDefaults() returned early without updating old bestiary entries that stored free-text capacity strings (e.g. 'Vole un objet mineur.'). The new MonsterEditor editor-side fallback (free-text → 'aucune') then rendered 'Aucune' for every affected library entry.
bugs.fix: Added a migration pass inside seedDefaults() that runs even when the guard key is set. It scans all cache entries with a templateId, skips those already holding a valid MonsterCapacityId, and updates the rest from the corresponding template. Self-limiting: after all entries are migrated the pass becomes a no-op. (src/brain/MonsterLibraryService.ts)
bugs.mitigation: The migration is tied to templateId + the registry validity check, so it cannot mutate user-authored monsters (those have no templateId). Future schema migrations of bestiary-templated entries should use the same seedDefaults migration-pass pattern rather than a separate migration step.
bugs.regression_test: src/brain/MonsterLibraryService.test.ts — 'seedDefaults() migrates legacy free-text capacity to registry id on subsequent launches (BUG)'

bugs.symptom: Vol de vie (Vampire) healed only half the damage dealt instead of the full damage, contradicting the spec entry 'Récupère autant de PV qu'il inflige de dégâts'.
bugs.root_cause: capacityEffects.ts used Math.floor(damage/2) instead of damage in the vol-de-vie onMonsterWon hook — a V1 overly-cautious simplification that was not aligned with the registry descriptor.
bugs.fix: Changed heal = Math.floor(damage / 2) to heal = damage in CAPACITY_HOOKS['vol-de-vie'].onMonsterWon (src/player/engine/capacityEffects.ts:524). Updated test expectation from 13 to 16 for a 6-damage hit with 10 starting PV.
bugs.mitigation: Always cross-check hook implementations against the descriptor text in MONSTER_CAPACITIES (brain/monsterCapacities.ts). The descriptor is the authoritative rule text; the hook is the implementation. Mismatches surface during self-review by comparing comment vs code.
bugs.regression_test: src/player/engine/capacityEffects.test.ts — 'vol-de-vie heals monster by the full damage dealt'

bugs.symptom: combatEngine.ts locally re-declared type HitQuality, duplicating the canonical export from brain/combat.ts. No runtime bug but a DRY violation and drift risk.
bugs.root_cause: Initial implementation omitted the import of HitQuality from brain/combat.ts and re-declared it locally instead.
bugs.fix: Added HitQuality to the type import from '../../brain/combat' in combatEngine.ts and removed the local const HIT_ORDER as const / type HitQuality declaration, replacing it with a plain HitQuality[] array.
bugs.mitigation: When adding types already exported from brain/, always import from the canonical source rather than re-declaring locally.
bugs.regression_test: tsc --noEmit (type check only, no runtime regression)

bugs.symptom: Tech-lead review: `applyCaracUpgrade('EN', hero)` incremented `pvMax` (FO+AG+EN) but NOT `peMax`, even though the rules define peMax = EN (§ 1). Upgrading EN via the XP shop would silently leave peMax stale.
bugs.root_cause: `applyCaracUpgrade` computed `pvMaxDelta` for FO/AG/EN but had no corresponding branch for `peMaxDelta`. The `computeCaracUpgrade` return type (`CaracUpgradeInfo`) also lacked `peMaxDelta`.
bugs.fix: Added `peMaxDelta: number` to `CaracUpgradeInfo` (1 when carac === 'EN', else 0). `applyCaracUpgrade` now applies `peMax: hero.peMax + peMaxDelta`. Added regression tests: 'increases peMax when upgrading EN' and 'does not change peMax for non-EN caracs'.
bugs.mitigation: KR-140: EN carac upgrade must always increment both pvMax and peMax. Any future stat-mutation function must cross-check all derived maximums (pvMax = FO+AG+EN; peMax = EN) against the rule sheet (§ 1).
bugs.regression_test: src/player/engine/actionEngine.test.ts — 'increases peMax when upgrading EN (peMax = EN, § 1)'

bugs.symptom: Tech-lead review: `recalcPvMax` was exported from `actionEngine.ts` but never imported by any consumer. Dead export with an unused `maxPV` import from `brain/xp`.
bugs.root_cause: Initial design extracted `recalcPvMax` as a helper anticipating reuse, but the callers inside `applyCaracUpgrade` were folded inline during implementation. The export was never removed.
bugs.fix: Removed `recalcPvMax` export and the now-unused `maxPV` import from `actionEngine.ts`.
bugs.mitigation: Before exporting a new function, verify at least one external caller exists. Dead exports are noise that misleads callers about the public API surface.
bugs.regression_test: tsc --noEmit (dead export removed; no runtime regression)
